Container.Name: ModelHub
Container.Overview:
Self-hosted, open 3D print file library manager: STL/3MF/OBJ/STEP/FBX organization, thumbnails, duplicate detection, tagging, semantic search, smart collections, filament inventory and a print queue. AI tagging/search can run against a local Ollama instance (nothing leaves your network) or an external OpenRouter/OpenAI-compatible API using your own key -- switch anytime from the in-app Settings tab. Point "Library Path" at the share where your STL/3MF files already live; nothing is modified on disk, files are only read and hashed.
On first open you'll be asked to create an admin login (or set Admin Username/Password below to skip that screen). Also includes print time/filament weight estimates, projects that track the electronics/parts/supplies each build needs (with an exportable shopping list and a Supplies page for what you already own) and subtract the filament used when a project is marked printed, matching of your models (one by one or your whole library) to their Printables/MakerWorld listings (pictures, designer, license, tags, parts lists), a page for every model and project with PDF export, a browser extension for one-click import, and optional webhook notifications (ntfy/Discord/Slack).
Container.Changes:
### 2.1.0 New Search tab: search your library and every connected site at once, open any result for a full preview page, and add models to your library with one click, or tick several and add them together (Printables and Thingiverse files are downloaded by the server, kept to model file types only, and linked to their listing with pictures and details). MyMiniFactory and Cults3D can now be searched too: add their API keys in Settings, where each site has a Test button. Settings also lets you download the browser extension, which now works on Thingiverse, MyMiniFactory, Cults3D and Sketchfab pages as well (and in Firefox), and downloads with your own login for sites that need it. Matches has a Linked models list that can unlink many models at once. No new settings are required; new tables and columns are added automatically on first start.
### 2.0.0 Every model and every project now has its own page instead of a popup (the back button works, and each page has an address you can bookmark). The model page shows the 3D view, details, editable tags, notes, its online listing, and the projects and collections it belongs to. The project page has an editable name, description and notes, its models with pictures and filament, the parts list, and an Export PDF button that makes a one-file summary of the whole project. The library now only lists and imports model files (.stl .3mf .obj .step .stp .fbx): zips, notes and other files in the library folder are ignored, importing a zip keeps just the models inside, and Settings has a cleanup for older entries. Model matching now also searches Sketchfab, and Thingiverse once you paste a free access token in Settings. The matching job can optionally link clear winners automatically (listed for a second look), and a project can use the filament a MakerWorld listing recommends, matched to your own spools. No new settings are required; new tables and columns are added automatically on first start.
### 1.9.0 New Matches tab: a background job searches Printables and MakerWorld for every model in your library that is not linked yet and builds a review queue of the closest listings. Link one, tick and link many at once, or mark a model as skipped; nothing is linked without your say-so. In a project you can now import the parts list from a MakerWorld listing (Bambu Lab store items with links and prices, plus the designer's own list), edit the rows, and add them in one go. Match thumbnails use small versions of the pictures, and the database now waits longer for a lock instead of failing while a background job is running. No settings changes; new tables are added automatically.
### 1.8.0 Shopping list export: download the Projects shopping list as CSV or text, or copy it, and optionally combine identical parts from different projects. New Supplies tab for the electronics, parts and supplies you already own, with low-stock flags, locations and CSV export; the shopping list shows how many you have in stock. Models can now be matched to their Printables or MakerWorld listing: search by name or paste a link, then pull in the title, designer, license, description, tags and pictures (pictures are shrunk and saved under /config/source_images). Models imported with the browser extension from those sites are matched automatically. The library API now returns each model's tags, so tags show up in the viewer. No settings changes; new tables and columns are added automatically on first start.
### 1.7.1 Fixes the browser holding on to the previous version's page after an upgrade (new tabs and features not showing up until a manual hard refresh). The page and its scripts are now versioned, and the server tells browsers to check for changes before reusing cached files, so updates appear on the next page load. No settings changes.
### 1.7.0 New Projects tab. A project groups library models and keeps a parts list (electronics, parts, supplies) with how many are needed vs. owned, unit cost and a buy link. Filter to the projects that still need parts, or open the Shopping List for everything missing across unfinished projects with an estimated total. Add a model to a project from its viewer, then give it one or more filament spools with grams each (the Estimate button fills grams from the print estimate). When a project is set to printed (or done) that filament is subtracted from inventory exactly once; moving it back to planning or building restores it. No new settings; new tables are created automatically on first start.
### 1.6.0 Fixes the app still crashing when a scan runs. Loading a model file takes many times its size in memory (a 35MB Bambu Studio project needed 4GB, a 262MB STL 3GB), and that happened inside the app itself -- one large file anywhere in the library could get the whole container killed on every scan. Model files are now parsed in a separate, memory-limited worker process: if a file is too big it's indexed from a preview instead (the .3mf's embedded thumbnail, or a streamed render of the STL), and if the worker dies anyway only that file is affected. New optional setting: Mesh Worker Memory (MB), blank for automatic. Thumbnail regeneration gets the same protection, and the 3D viewer now asks before loading huge models.
### 1.5.0 Fixes an OOM crash loop and a 3D viewer error on multi-part .3mf project files (Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer, which split each plate/object into its own file inside the .3mf). Scanning one of these could consume 15GB+ of RAM computing mesh watertightness and OOM-kill the container on every launch -- since the background scan runs on startup, this could look like the app crashing right after launching, and any files past that one in scan order (including in subfolders -- scanning was already recursive, it just never got that far) would never get indexed. Also extracts the slicer's own embedded preview from .3mf files when present instead of rendering our own, and fixes the live 3D viewer failing to open these same multi-part files.
### 1.4.0 Fixes the actual root cause of Tag All crashing the container: an oversized AI response (e.g. a local vision model stuck generating past a sane length) could get fully buffered into memory in a single network call fast enough to OOM the container in seconds -- too fast for the 1.3.0 fix's periodic checkpointing to help. AI responses are now streamed with a hard size cap so that can't happen, generation length is capped as a second line of defense, and the tagging job now checks the container's actual memory usage before every model and stops itself cleanly (instead of the kernel silently killing the container) if it's running critically high.
### 1.3.0 Tag All no longer risks crashing/hanging on large untagged libraries: the batch job now periodically releases database state instead of holding everything in memory for the whole run, per-model failures are logged instead of silently swallowed, and a crash mid-job no longer leaves the tagging state stuck. Also adds a configurable 3D preview/thumbnail color (Settings -> 3D Preview) plus a Regenerate Thumbnails maintenance job (contributed by @justindgreen), which runs in parallel and can resume if interrupted.
### 1.2.0 Large-library fixes contributed by @justindgreen: the initial/background scan now runs off the main event loop so the WebUI and health check come up immediately instead of appearing stuck on big libraries; mesh/thumbnail memory use is now bounded so indexing a large library no longer grows memory unboundedly; concurrent scans are rejected cleanly instead of racing on SQLite; the Library view is now paginated with full-library search instead of only showing the first 200 models.
### 1.1.0 Live STEP/STP viewer (client-side WASM via occt-import-js, no server round trip), rate limiting on the login endpoint (5 attempts / 15 min per IP), and a mobile-responsive UI (scrollable tab bar, stacked forms, full-screen viewer modal, larger touch targets).
### 1.0.0 Initial release. STL/3MF/OBJ/FBX live viewer, AI auto-tagging + semantic search (local Ollama or API), smart collections, filament inventory, print queue with volumetric/slicer-based estimates, session auth, webhook notifications, a Printables/MakerWorld browser extension, and PUID/PGID support so files under /config are owned by a real host user instead of root.
Container.Requires: Optional: an Ollama container (install the official "ollama" template from Community Applications first) if you want local AI instead of an API key.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the Model Hub web interface

Config.Name: Library Path
Config.Description: Folder containing your STL/3MF/OBJ/STEP/FBX files. Read-only usage: files are hashed and thumbnailed, never modified.

Config.Name: App Config/DB
Config.Description: Where the SQLite database, thumbnails, and settings are stored.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: Unraid's nobody user -- keeps /config editable from the host

Config.Name: Scan Interval
Config.Description: Seconds between automatic background library scans.

Config.Name: Mesh Worker Memory (MB)
Config.Description: Memory ceiling for the separate process that parses model files during scans. Leave blank for automatic (half of the container limit or host RAM, 1-8 GB). Files needing more are still indexed, from a preview (a .3mf's embedded thumbnail, or a streamed render of an STL) instead of a full parse. Raise it only if you have RAM to spare and want full stats on very large files.

Config.Name: Ollama Host
Config.Description: Address of your Ollama container/instance for local AI tagging. Only used when AI mode is set to 'local' in the app's Settings tab.

Config.Name: Ollama Vision Model
Config.Description: Vision-capable Ollama model used for auto-tagging thumbnails.

Config.Name: Ollama Embed Model
Config.Description: Ollama embedding model used for semantic search.

Config.Name: Admin Username
Config.Description: Creates the admin login automatically on first start. Leave blank to set it up from the WebUI's first-run screen instead.

Config.Name: Admin Password
Config.Description: Paired with Admin Username above. Leave both blank to use the in-app setup screen instead (recommended -- avoids the password sitting in plain text in the container's env).

Config.Name: Slicer CLI Path (advanced)
Config.Description: Optional: absolute path *inside the container* to a headless slicer CLI binary (e.g. an extracted PrusaSlicer/OrcaSlicer AppImage) for exact print time/filament estimates instead of the built-in volumetric approximation. Bind-mount the binary in via 'Add another Path' first, then point this at it.
